what_it_is.prose: Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited (KSSL), a Kalyani Group company under Bharat Forge, lists three Air Defence products on its official page: Close-In Weapon Station (CIWS), Army AD Gun (replacement of L-70 and ZU-23), and SPIKE ATGM (manufactured under licence from Rafael Advanced Defense Systems). The 'Bharat CUAS' configuration referenced in the Atlas corresponds most plausibly to a proposed Kalyani M4 vehicle-based CUAS configuration reported by IDRW in December 2025. The proposed configuration includes a mast-mounted multi-sensor array (passive RF detectors, compact 3D radar, EO/IR trackers), directional jammers, laser dazzlers, and three hard-kill effectors: a 7.62 mm coaxial Light Machine Gun with smart air-burst ammunition, a 40 mm Automatic Grenade Launcher with proximity-fused rounds, and a 113 mm multi-barrel cannon 'specifically optimised for high-volume, rapid-response fire against Group 1 and Group 2 drones' engaging swarms at ranges beyond 3 km while the vehicle remains mobile. The Indian Army's Directorate of Mechanised Forces and Northern Command were reported in December 2025 to be 'actively evaluating' the configuration. No production contract has been signed. The Kalyani M4 base vehicle is a licensed derivative of the Paramount Group (South Africa) Mbombe 4, customised in India by Bharat Forge.

deployments_procurement.summary: The Indian Army's Directorate of Mechanised Forces and Northern Command were reported in December 2025 to be evaluating the proposed Kalyani M4 CUAS configuration. No production contract has been signed. The KSSL CIWS (a separate product) is described as a 'proven solution' but specific customer deployments are not publicly itemised.
